root_cause.text: The absence of a capability check (CAP_NET_RAW) when setting IPv4 source routing options (SSRR/LSRR) allowed unprivileged users to set these options and force packets through attacker-controlled paths, enabling TCP ISN leakage.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (opt->opt.srr && !ns_capable(net->user_ns, CAP_NET_RAW))` in `ip_options_get()` to reject setting source route options without CAP_NET_RAW. The CVE and commit message explicitly state that unprivileged applications could use LSRR/SSRR to leak TCP ISN and other protocol information.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add capability check to prevent unprivileged users from setting IP source route options via ip_options_get.
intent_record.what: Added a check after validating IP options: if the source route option (srr) is set and the caller does not have CAP_NET_RAW in the network namespace, free the option and return -EPERM.
intent_record.how: The function now rejects setting source route options unless the caller has CAP_NET_RAW capability, preventing unprivileged users from enabling source routing.

candidates.rationale: This assignment makes the IP source route options effective without a preceding capability check, allowing unprivileged users to set source routing.

vuln_statements.explanation: The assignment makes the IP source route options effective without a preceding capability check, allowing unprivileged users to set source routing and cause TCP ISN leakage.

bic_trace_step.reason: In `ip_options_compile()`, the case for IPOPT_SSRR and IPOPT_LSRR does not include a capability check (`capable(CAP_NET_RAW)`) when `!skb` (i.e., when called from user space via `ip_options_get`). Other options like IPOPT_TIMESTAMP and IPOPT_SEC have such a check (lines with `if (!skb && !capable(CAP_NET_RAW))`), but SSRR/LSRR are missing it, allowing unprivileged users to set source routing options. No fix is present in this commit.
